_notes.source: Lane copy artifact UAY5Jp9xRL2zM8PtCXRNu9, version 7, with the fixes agreed 2026-10-01.
_notes.review_removed: cr, dm1 and em1 opened on 'your review caught my eye'. {review_site} had no data source and only 19 of 160 left a review, so Act 1 now stands on the price rise, which is true for all 160 confirmed Harvest users.
_notes.signature: {signature} is substituted per campaign at load time (Sina or Denzel). It is never a per-lead value because each campaign has exactly one owner.
_notes.cr_is_ab: cr carries two variants. It is the step the most people see, so it is the most informative place to test.
_notes.inmail: Mirrors the DM arc message for message so the argument does not change with whether someone accepted the connection request. Only inmail1 differs from its DM, because dm1 opens on the accepted connection and these recipients never accepted one.
_notes.demo_link: Built per lead by the push: the TP4 landing page with campaign=harvest, the owner presenter and booking link, and the contact email so the visit is attributed. Not a constant, because of the email.
_notes.dm1: Sina's draft, second paragraph smoothed 2026-10-01. Act 1 now makes lane A's argument (the disconnected stack) and lane B's (AI on one source of truth), both deliberately. Those two lanes therefore re-state in week 2 something every contact already read in week 1, which weakens the A/B/C comparison: only lane C's angle is new to its readers.
_notes.act1: Sina's final Act 1, 2026-10-01, same words on both channels. The LinkedIn version opens on the accepted connection; the email cannot, because it is not conditional on one. Act 1 makes lane A's argument (the disconnected stack) and lane B's (AI on one source of truth), so both re-state in week 2 something every contact already read. Chosen deliberately.

cr.A: Hi {first_name}, I've been speaking with a lot of firms who were with Harvest for years and then had a steep price rise they had no say in. A few have told me the same story. WorkflowMAX may be worth a look. I'd love to connect either way.
cr.B: Hi {first_name}, a lot of Harvest users have been shocked by the recent pricing changes after years as customers. Putting WorkflowMAX on your radar, not just another time tracker but an OS that runs the whole job, lead to invoice. Love to connect either way.
cr.C: Hi {first_name}, I've been speaking with firms who have been on Harvest a long time and have just seen what the new pricing looks like. For a few it has been enough to start looking properly. WorkflowMAX might be worth a look. Happy to connect either way.

dm1:
Hi {first_name}, thanks for connecting.

I imagine you have been on Harvest a number of years, and the recent price rise may have felt quite shocking. For most businesses it has been enough to start looking.

While you may be looking, I wanted to put WorkflowMAX on your radar. Even before this price increase, firms have come to us as a step up from Harvest, because what is on offer is not just another simple timesheet and invoicing tool. We bring the whole job lifecycle into one place, from the lead through to the final invoice.

And once one system holds the whole story, you can connect it to the AI tool you use every day and just ask about your jobs and your numbers, rather than digging through reports.

You may have this down better than most, but the most common set up I see is quotes in a spreadsheet, proposals in a Word doc, and time and costs in Harvest, disconnected from what was actually sold. That cannot tell you how a job is tracking while there is still time to steer it. I put the two side by side here: https://wfmax.info/2wvwsza6

Open to a chat about what this shift could look like for your business?

dm2.A:
{first_name}, following on from my last note. The pricing is reason enough to be looking, you do not need me to tell you that. What is worth knowing while you are looking is what else is costing you, because it rarely shows up on a licence line. Leads in a CRM, quoting in a spreadsheet, purchase orders and bills in an inbox, and someone reconciling it all by hand before the numbers mean anything.

With WorkflowMAX the lead, the quote, the job, the costs and the invoice are one record, all there for you to ask about with your AI tool. Here is a walkthrough. {demo_link}
dm2.B:
{first_name}, picking up the AI point from my last note. The tools are fine, the limit is usually what they can read. If the fee proposal sits in one system and the time and costs in another, there is nothing holding a whole project for an assistant to answer from.

With WorkflowMAX the lead, the quote, the job, the costs and the invoice are one record, so you can just ask it what is due to invoice, or which clients actually made money. Here is a walkthrough. {demo_link}
dm2.C:
{first_name}, one more thing from my last note. The other place margin goes is variations. The extra round gets done, nobody logs it because logging it is admin, and by the time it surfaces at month end it is too late to put on an invoice.

With WorkflowMAX you can manage variations as they happen, invoice a percentage of progress against the proposal, and see WIP clearly, so scope creep gets caught while the job is still running. Here is a quick walkthrough. {demo_link}

dm3:
{first_name}, we know change is hard. That's why we've saved the best for last.

We have built a migration tool specifically for Harvest. Start a trial, connect your account, and your own clients, jobs and time history come across in a few minutes. Not a demo running on someone else's data, your own work, sitting in a system that can do a good deal more with it.

There is no risk. Nothing changes on the Harvest side while you trial, it is a copy rather than a move.

Happy to sit on a call and go through it with you, or send you the steps if you would rather have a poke at it yourself. {trial_link}

A.subject: The costs that don't show on a licence
A.body:
Hi {first_name},

The price rise is reason enough to be looking, and you do not need me to explain that one to you.

What is worth knowing while you are looking is what else is costing you, because it rarely shows up on a licence line. Leads sitting in a CRM, quoting done in a spreadsheet, purchase orders and bills in an inbox, and somebody reconciling all of it by hand before anyone can say how a project actually went without relying on a bank balance.

That is what changes with WorkflowMAX. The lead, the quote, the job, the costs and the invoice are one record, all of it there for you to ask about with your AI tool.

See it for yourself here.

{demo_link}

{signature}

B.subject: The question your AI can't answer

C.subject: The extra round nobody billed
C.body:
Hi {first_name},

Most firms can tell you exactly what they quoted. Far fewer can tell you what they actually delivered.

The extra iteration, the revised option, the bit redone after the client changed their mind. It all gets done, most of it gets absorbed, and the decision about whether to bill it happens weeks after the work did. The same gap shows up again as work in progress that nobody can see until month end.

With WorkflowMAX you are not just bringing the whole job lifecycle under one roof. You can manage variations as they happen, invoice a percentage of progress against the original proposal, and see WIP clearly, so scope creep gets caught while the job is still running rather than after it. And all of it can be pulled up by prompting your AI tool rather than building a report.

Here is a quick walkthrough of it all for you.

{demo_link}

{signature}

em4.subject: Last one from me
em4.body:
Hi {first_name},

I have sent a few things this month and have not heard back, which usually means the timing is wrong or it simply is not a priority right now. Both are completely fair, and I will stop here rather than keep turning up.

Two things worth keeping hold of either way.

Our pricing is published on our website, per user per month, and there is nothing in it based on invoice counts or invoiced value.

And the Harvest migration tool is not going anywhere. If you decide to look in three months, connecting your account and seeing your own data takes the same few minutes then as it does today.

{trial_link}

Thanks for your time.

{signature}
